discovery: Precision mapping of the cosmic microwave background anisotropies with WMAP, establishing the standard ΛCDM cosmological model
motivation: The Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe turned cosmology into a precision science. Bennett led the mission, Page led the design and calibration of its differential radiometers, and Spergel led the cosmological interpretation. WMAP produced full-sky, systematics-controlled maps of CMB temperature and polarization anisotropies. From them came percent-level measurements of the Universe's age, geometry, and matter and dark-energy content, and of the primordial fluctuations. These measurements agreed with supernova and galaxy-clustering data and established the six-parameter ΛCDM model. WMAP's first-year polarization data detected reionization, and its data showed the nearly scale-invariant, Gaussian, adiabatic spectrum that inflation predicts. Its public data releases and analysis methods set the standard for later work, including Planck, DESI and Euclid. Today every test of new physics, including the Hubble tension, is measured against the standard model that WMAP established. The 2006 Prize recognized COBE's detection of the anisotropies. WMAP's precise characterization of them now deserves the same recognition.
